pharm-endo:endomap.q: A 31-year-old woman with untreated Graves disease presents after a urinary infection with fever 40 °C, HR 150/min, agitation and vomiting. Propylthiouracil is chosen over methimazole. Which additional action explains this choice?
pharm-endo:endomap.e: In thyroid storm, PTU also blocks peripheral T₄→T₃ conversion. Blocking iodide release from thyroglobulin is the action of iodide or lithium, not thionamides.

pharm-endo:insulin.q: Which insulin has the fastest onset?
pharm-endo:insulin.e: Rapid-acting analogs are given with meals.
Used to treat hyperkalemia with glucose.

pharm-endo:insulin.q: A 19-year-old man with type 1 diabetes has vomiting and Kussmaul breathing. Glucose 540 mg/dL, pH 7.12, HCO₃⁻ 9 mEq/L, anion gap 26, K⁺ 3.1 mEq/L. IV normal saline is started. What is the best next step?
pharm-endo:insulin.e: Insulin drives K⁺ into cells and could cause dangerous hypokalemia; with K⁺ < 3.3 mEq/L, replete potassium first. Bicarbonate is not indicated at pH 7.12.

pharm-endo:sensitizer.e: Weight gain, edema, HF exacerbation, fractures. PPAR-γ activation ↑ insulin sensitivity.

pharm-endo:sensitizer.q: A 63-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes started an oral drug 4 months ago. She has gained 5 kg and now has ankle edema, orthopnea and bibasal crackles; HbA1c has improved from 8.4% to 7.1%. What is this drug's molecular target?
pharm-endo:sensitizer.e: Thiazolidinediones (pioglitazone) activate PPAR-γ, causing fluid retention and HF exacerbation. PPAR-α is the fibrate target.

pharm-endo:secretagog.e: Require functioning β cells. Depolarization → Ca²⁺ influx → insulin release.

pharm-endo:secretagog.q: A major adverse effect of sulfonylureas:
pharm-endo:secretagog.e: Especially glyburide in the elderly and renal impairment.

pharm-endo:secretagog.q: A 77-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and eGFR 32 mL/min had a second oral agent added to metformin last month. He is found confused at 3 a.m. with glucose 36 mg/dL; serum insulin and C-peptide are both elevated. Which drug was most likely added?
pharm-endo:secretagog.e: High insulin and C-peptide mean endogenous insulin secretion, as with sulfonylureas; glyburide is long-acting with active renally cleared metabolites. DPP-4 inhibitors rarely cause hypoglycemia alone.

pharm-endo:incretin.e: Weight neutral; mild URIs, possible pancreatitis.
Slows gastric emptying, ↓ glucagon; used with insulin.

pharm-endo:incretin.q: A 52-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and obesity starts a once-weekly subcutaneous injection; over 3 months she loses 6 kg with mild nausea. She then presents with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and lipase 900 U/L. What is the mechanism of the drug?
pharm-endo:incretin.e: Weekly injectable GLP-1 agonists (semaglutide, dulaglutide) cause weight loss and GI effects and are linked to pancreatitis. DPP-4 inhibitors are oral and weight neutral.

o: Inhibiting renal SGLT2 in the PCT

pharm-endo:glucose-other.q: Hypoglycemia in a patient on acarbose plus a sulfonylurea should be treated with:

A 54-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes takes metformin and empagliflozin. On day 1 after surgery, fasting, she has nausea and rapid breathing: glucose 186 mg/dL, pH 7.17, HCO₃⁻ 11 mEq/L, anion gap 24, serum β-hydroxybutyrate markedly raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?
pharm-endo:glucose-other.e: SGLT2 inhibitors can cause ketoacidosis with near-normal glucose, especially with fasting or surgery. Starvation ketosis does not cause this degree of acidosis.

pharm-endo:thionamide.q: Thionamide preferred in the first trimester of pregnancy:
pharm-endo:thionamide.e: Methimazole is teratogenic early (aplasia cutis); PTU is hepatotoxic.

pharm-endo:thionamide.q: Serious adverse effect of both thionamides:
pharm-endo:thionamide.e: Check CBC if fever or sore throat.

pharm-endo:thionamide.q: A 32-year-old woman with Graves disease started methimazole 6 weeks ago. She now has fever 39 °C and a sore throat; absolute neutrophil count is 300/µL. What is the most appropriate next step regarding her thyroid drug?
pharm-endo:thionamide.e: Thionamide agranulocytosis requires stopping the drug; switching to PTU is unsafe because of cross-reactivity. Definitive therapy (radioiodine or surgery) is planned instead.

pharm-endo:thyroxine.q: TSH is used to titrate levothyroxine in primary hypothyroidism because:
o: T₄ feeds back on the pituitary
pharm-endo:thyroxine.e: Recheck TSH 6–8 weeks after a dose change.

pharm-endo:thyroxine.q: A 70-year-old woman with hypothyroidism has had TSH in range on levothyroxine for years. After she begins taking calcium carbonate and ferrous sulfate with her morning levothyroxine, TSH rises to 12 mU/L. What best explains the change?
pharm-endo:thyroxine.e: Calcium, iron and binders chelate levothyroxine in the gut; separate doses by ≥ 4 hours. Raised TBG (e.g., pregnancy, estrogen) also raises needs, but not with these supplements.

pharm-endo:pituitary.e: ADH (V₂) receptor antagonists; avoid rapid correction of Na⁺ (osmotic demyelination).

pharm-endo:pituitary.q: A 25-year-old man develops polyuria of 6 L/day after a head injury. Serum Na⁺ is 148 mEq/L and urine osmolality 120 mOsm/kg; after a dose of desmopressin, urine osmolality rises to 460 mOsm/kg. How does this drug concentrate his urine?
pharm-endo:pituitary.e: Response to desmopressin confirms central DI; the V₂ agonist raises cAMP and inserts aquaporin-2 into collecting-duct membranes. V₁ effects are vascular.

pharm-endo:adrenal.e: Synthetic mineralocorticoid — replaces aldosterone in primary adrenal insufficiency.

pharm-endo:adrenal.q: Glucocorticoid withdrawal after long-term use risks:
pharm-endo:adrenal.e: HPA axis suppression; taper the dose.

pharm-endo:adrenal.q: A 38-year-old woman has fatigue, weight loss and darkened skin creases. BP is 88/56 mm Hg; Na⁺ 128 mEq/L, K⁺ 5.8 mEq/L; morning cortisol is low and ACTH markedly elevated. Which long-term regimen is most appropriate?
pharm-endo:adrenal.e: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison) lacks both cortisol and aldosterone, so both are replaced. Hydrocortisone alone does not fully correct hyperkalemia and volume loss.

pharm-endo:calcium.q: Sevelamer is used in CKD to:

pharm-endo:calcium.e: Used for secondary hyperparathyroidism and parathyroid carcinoma.

pharm-endo:calcium.q: A 66-year-old man with stage 3b CKD (eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73 m²) and HFrEF on lisinopril and spironolactone has repeated K⁺ of 5.3–5.5 mEq/L with a normal ECG. His physician wants to continue both drugs. Which addition is most appropriate?
pharm-endo:calcium.e: Patiromer is a colonic K⁺-binding (Ca²⁺-exchange) resin that permits continued RAAS inhibition. Sevelamer binds phosphate, not potassium.

pharm-endo:dmrx.q: HbA1c target for most nonpregnant adults:
pharm-endo:dmrx.e: Individualize for frail elderly and hypoglycemia risk.

pharm-endo:dmrx.q: For type 2 diabetes with CKD, which class slows kidney disease progression?

A 67-year-old man with type 2 diabetes has taken the usual first-line oral agent for 10 years. He has numbness in both feet, reduced vibration sense and Hb 10.8 g/dL with MCV 108 fL; serum B12 is low. Which drug is the most likely contributor?
pharm-endo:dmrx.e: Long-term metformin impairs ileal B12 absorption; check B12 periodically. Neuropathy alone could be diabetic, but macrocytic anemia with low B12 points to metformin.

endo-patho-1:pit-adenoma.q: The most common hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma is the:
endo-patho-1:pit-adenoma.e: Prolactin-secreting adenomas make up about 30% of clinically recognized adenomas.

endo-patho-1:pit-adenoma.q: Which histologic feature best separates a pituitary adenoma from normal anterior pituitary?
o: Monomorphic cells without a reticulin network
Mixed cell types within a reticulin framework
endo-patho-1:pit-adenoma.e: Normal gland is a mix of cell types held in a reticulin network.

endo-patho-1:pit-adenoma.q: A 52-year-old man has headaches and bumps into door frames. Prolactin is mildly elevated. MRI shows a 2.8-cm sellar mass that stains for FSH and LH but causes no hormone excess syndrome. Why is prolactin raised?
o: Compression of the stalk interrupts dopamine delivery
Hypothyroidism from the mass raises TRH
The tumor cells are co-secreting prolactin
endo-patho-1:pit-adenoma.e: Stalk effect: any suprasellar mass can lift dopamine inhibition of lactotrophs.

o: Hypovolemic hyponatremia with urine sodium below 20
Euvolemic hyponatremia with urine osmolality above serum
endo-patho-1:siadh.e: Free water retention with continued urinary Na⁺ loss.

endo-patho-1:siadh.q: The first-line treatment of chronic asymptomatic SIADH is:
endo-patho-1:siadh.e: Then urea or tolvaptan if restriction fails; hypertonic saline only for severe neurologic symptoms.

endo-patho-1:siadh.q: A 64-year-old smoker has confusion. Serum Na⁺ is 121 mEq/L, serum osmolality 250 mOsm/kg, urine osmolality 520 mOsm/kg and urine Na⁺ 58 mmol/L. He has no edema and normal orthostatic vitals. A chest mass is found. The most likely cause of his hyponatremia is:
o: Volume depletion from poor oral intake
Ectopic ADH from small cell carcinoma
endo-patho-1:siadh.e: Euvolemic hyponatremia with concentrated urine and high urine Na⁺ = SIADH.

endo-patho-1:di.q: During water deprivation, urine osmolality rises above 700 mOsm/kg. The diagnosis is most likely:
endo-patho-1:di.e: Intact ADH secretion and renal response concentrate the urine.

endo-patho-1:di.q: Which drug classically causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus?
endo-patho-1:di.e: Demeclocycline, hypercalcemia and hypokalemia also cause ADH resistance; the others cause SIADH.

endo-patho-1:di.q: Two days after transsphenoidal surgery, a 41-year-old woman passes 6 L of urine a day. Serum Na⁺ is 149 mEq/L and urine osmolality is 140 mOsm/kg. After desmopressin, urine osmolality rises to 410 mOsm/kg. The best long-term treatment is:
endo-patho-1:di.e: A >50% rise after desmopressin indicates central DI.

endo-patho-1:hypopit.q: In Sheehan syndrome the posterior pituitary is usually spared because it:
endo-patho-1:hypopit.e: The enlarged anterior lobe depends on a low-pressure portal venous supply.

endo-patho-1:hypopit.q: Hypopituitarism accompanied by diabetes insipidus most strongly suggests disease of the:
endo-patho-1:hypopit.e: ADH is made in the hypothalamus; isolated anterior lobe disease spares it.

endo-patho-1:hypopit.q: A 29-year-old woman bled heavily during delivery and needed 6 units of blood. Six weeks later she cannot breastfeed, feels cold all the time and has not menstruated. The most likely mechanism is:
o: Herniation of CSF through the diaphragma sellae
Ischemic necrosis of the enlarged anterior pituitary
Autoimmune lymphocytic destruction of the pituitary
endo-patho-1:hypopit.e: Sheehan syndrome: postpartum infarction of the anterior lobe.

endo-patho-1:acro.q: The best screening test for acromegaly is serum:
endo-patho-1:acro.e: GH is pulsatile; IGF-1 integrates GH secretion. Confirm with failure of GH suppression after oral glucose.

endo-patho-1:acro.q: The most common cause of death in acromegaly is:
endo-patho-1:acro.e: LVH, cardiomyopathy and HFpEF; cardiovascular and cerebrovascular causes dominate.

endo-patho-1:acro.q: A 47-year-old man needs larger shoes and his wedding ring no longer fits. He has a large tongue, wide spacing of the lower teeth and new hyperglycemia. After a 75-g glucose load, GH stays at 9 µg/L. If surgery does not cure him, which drug blocks the hormone's peripheral action?
endo-patho-1:acro.e: Pegvisomant is a GH receptor antagonist; octreotide and dopamine agonists reduce GH secretion.

endo-patho-1:thy-func.q: Proptosis caused by retro-orbital tissue expansion is seen only in:
endo-patho-1:thy-func.e: Lid lag and stare occur in any thyrotoxicosis from sympathetic overactivity.

endo-patho-1:thy-func.q: Myxedema in hypothyroidism is caused by accumulation of:
endo-patho-1:thy-func.e: Hydrophilic GAGs and hyaluronic acid cause nonpitting edema.

endo-patho-1:thy-func.q: A 78-year-old woman has lost 6 kg and has new atrial fibrillation but appears listless rather than anxious. TSH is undetectable and free T4 is high. This presentation is best termed:
endo-patho-1:thy-func.e: Older patients may have blunted adrenergic features of thyrotoxicosis.

endo-patho-1:thy-labs.q: The single most sensitive screening test for primary thyroid dysfunction is:
endo-patho-1:thy-labs.e: TSH changes early, even in subclinical disease.

endo-patho-1:thy-labs.q: A low free T4 with a low-normal TSH points to:
endo-patho-1:thy-labs.e: The pituitary fails to raise TSH despite low hormone.

endo-patho-1:thy-labs.q: A 55-year-old man in the ICU with septic shock has low T3, low-normal T4 and a normal TSH. He has no thyroid history. The best interpretation is:
endo-patho-1:thy-labs.e: Euthyroid sick syndrome; treat the illness, not the labs.

endo-patho-1:thyroiditis.q: Hürthle cells and lymphoid follicles with germinal centers are characteristic of:
endo-patho-1:thyroiditis.e: Hürthle cells are eosinophilic metaplasia of injured follicular epithelium.

endo-patho-1:thyroiditis.q: Riedel thyroiditis belongs to the spectrum of:
endo-patho-1:thyroiditis.e: Fibrosis extends beyond the capsule and can mimic anaplastic carcinoma.

endo-patho-1:thyroiditis.q: Three weeks after a sore throat, a 38-year-old woman has fever, a very tender thyroid and pain radiating to her jaw. ESR is 92 mm/h; TSH is low and free T4 high. Radioiodine uptake would be:
endo-patho-1:thyroiditis.e: Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis: preformed hormone leaks from damaged follicles.

endo-patho-1:cong-hypo.q: In iodine-sufficient regions, congenital hypothyroidism is most often caused by:
endo-patho-1:cong-hypo.e: Agenesis, hypoplasia or ectopy; dyshormonogenesis is the next major group.

o: Inhibition of hormone synthesis by excess iodide
Low T3 in critically ill patients
endo-patho-1:cong-hypo.e: Jod-Basedow is the opposite: iodide load causing thyrotoxicosis.

endo-patho-1:cong-hypo.q: A 2-month-old infant missed newborn screening. She is lethargic and pale, with a large protruding tongue, puffy face and an umbilical hernia. Without treatment, the most serious long-term consequence is:
endo-patho-1:cong-hypo.e: Thyroid hormone is critical for early brain development.

o: Inhibiting deiodination of T4 to T3
Binding and activating the TSH receptor
endo-patho-1:graves.e: Type II hypersensitivity with a stimulatory antibody.

endo-patho-1:graves.q: Exophthalmos in Graves disease results mainly from:
o: Venous congestion from a large goiter
Thyroid hormone acting on orbital fat
Sympathetic contraction of the superior tarsal muscle
endo-patho-1:graves.e: T-cell cytokines drive GAG synthesis, edema and adipocyte increase.

endo-patho-1:graves.q: A 29-year-old woman has palpitations, weight loss, a diffuse goiter with a bruit and thickened, waxy skin over both shins. TSH is suppressed. A biopsy of the thyroid would most likely show:
o: Dense fibrosis extending into neck muscles
Atrophic follicles with Hürthle cell change
Tall crowded cells with scalloped pale colloid
endo-patho-1:graves.e: Graves: diffuse hyperplasia, scalloped colloid, lymphoid infiltrates.

endo-patho-1:thyrotox.q: Hot nodules in toxic multinodular goiter are often caused by:
endo-patho-1:thyrotox.e: Autonomous follicles work independently of TSH; they are rarely malignant.

endo-patho-1:thyrotox.q: In thyroid storm, iodide should be given:
o: After a thionamide has been started
endo-patho-1:thyrotox.e: Iodide first could feed new hormone synthesis; PTU also blocks T4→T3.

endo-patho-1:thyrotox.q: A 34-year-old woman trying to lose weight has tremor and tachycardia. TSH is undetectable and free T4 high. The thyroid is not enlarged and radioiodine uptake is low. Which serum finding would support the diagnosis?
endo-patho-1:thyrotox.e: Exogenous thyroxine suppresses the gland, so thyroglobulin is low (it is high in thyroiditis).

endo-patho-1:goiter.q: Most patients with a simple diffuse goiter are:
A follicular adenoma differs from follicular carcinoma by lacking:
endo-patho-1:goiter.e: FNA cannot make the distinction; the capsule must be examined after excision.

endo-patho-1:goiter.q: A 66-year-old woman has had a slowly enlarging, irregular neck mass for 20 years. It now extends behind the sternum and she has new dysphagia. TSH is low-normal. The gland is lumpy on both sides. The most likely diagnosis is:
endo-patho-1:goiter.e: Repeated hyperplasia and involution produce the largest, most irregular goiters.

endo-patho-1:thy-ca.q: Psammoma bodies and nuclei with clear, ground-glass chromatin indicate:
endo-patho-1:thy-ca.e: Orphan Annie nuclei and nuclear grooves are diagnostic even without papillae.

endo-patho-1:thy-ca.q: Which thyroid cancer typically spreads through the bloodstream to bone and lung?
endo-patho-1:thy-ca.e: Papillary spreads by lymphatics to cervical nodes.

endo-patho-1:thy-ca.q: A 31-year-old man has a thyroid nodule and a calcitonin level of 900 pg/mL. His father had surgery for an adrenal tumor that caused episodic headaches. Before thyroidectomy, which test is most important?
endo-patho-1:thy-ca.e: Medullary carcinoma suggests MEN2; a pheochromocytoma must be excluded before surgery.

endo-patho-1:nodule-wu.q: The first test in a patient with a thyroid nodule is:
endo-patho-1:nodule-wu.e: A low TSH directs to a scan; otherwise ultrasound and FNA by size and pattern.

endo-patho-1:nodule-wu.q: A hyperfunctioning (hot) thyroid nodule on scan should be managed by:
o: Repeat scan in five years only
endo-patho-1:nodule-wu.e: Hot nodules are almost never malignant.

endo-patho-1:nodule-wu.q: A 45-year-old woman has a 2.2-cm solid hypoechoic thyroid nodule with microcalcifications. TSH is normal. Ultrasound-guided FNA is reported as Bethesda IV (follicular neoplasm). The most appropriate next step is:
endo-patho-1:nodule-wu.e: FNA cannot exclude follicular carcinoma; molecular tests or diagnostic surgery decide.

endo-patho-1:sellar.q: Craniopharyngioma is derived from remnants of:
endo-patho-1:sellar.e: It usually lies above the sella.

endo-patho-1:sellar.q: Wet keratin and calcified cysts with machine-oil fluid indicate the:
endo-patho-1:sellar.e: Adamantinomatous type affects children and carries CTNNB1 mutations.

endo-patho-1:sellar.q: An 8-year-old boy has headaches, short stature and bitemporal visual field loss. CT shows a calcified cystic suprasellar mass. Which gene is most likely mutated in the tumor?
endo-patho-1:sellar.e: Childhood adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma; the adult papillary type carries BRAF V600E.

endo-patho-2:pth-map.q: High calcium with an inappropriately normal-high PTH indicates:
endo-patho-2:pth-map.e: In PTH-independent causes, high calcium suppresses PTH.

endo-patho-2:pth-map.q: In secondary hyperparathyroidism from chronic kidney disease, serum phosphate is typically:
endo-patho-2:pth-map.e: Other causes of 2° HPT (vitamin D deficiency, low intake) give low phosphate.

endo-patho-2:pth-map.q: A 62-year-old man on dialysis for 9 years has a calcium of 11.6 mg/dL, phosphate 6.8 mg/dL and PTH 1,450 pg/mL despite phosphate binders. Calcium stayed high after a kidney transplant. This is best termed:
endo-patho-2:pth-map.e: Long-standing 2° hyperplasia that has become autonomous.

endo-patho-2:hypopara.q: Pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A results from a maternally inherited defect in:
endo-patho-2:hypopara.e: Imprinting: kidney expresses mainly the maternal GNAS allele.
Albright osteodystrophy without end-organ PTH resistance.

endo-patho-2:hypopara.q: A 9-year-old boy with short stature, a round face and short fourth and fifth metacarpals has muscle cramps. Calcium is 6.9 mg/dL, phosphate 7.1 mg/dL and PTH 240 pg/mL. His father is unaffected; his mother has the same body habitus. The underlying problem is:

endo-patho-2:hypoca-labs.q: Which laboratory finding best separates vitamin D deficiency from hypoparathyroidism?
endo-patho-2:hypoca-labs.e: PTH is high in vitamin D deficiency and low in hypoparathyroidism.

endo-patho-2:hypoca-labs.q: In vitamin D deficiency, serum phosphate tends to be:
endo-patho-2:hypoca-labs.e: Poor gut absorption plus PTH-driven phosphaturia.

endo-patho-2:hypoca-labs.q: A 34-year-old woman had a total thyroidectomy 3 days ago and now has perioral tingling. Calcium is 7.0 mg/dL and phosphate 5.6 mg/dL. Which other finding is expected?
endo-patho-2:hypoca-labs.e: Without PTH the kidney retains phosphate and cannot activate vitamin D.

endo-patho-2:hyperpara.q: The most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism is:
endo-patho-2:hyperpara.e: Adenoma 85–95%; the other glands are often atrophic.

endo-patho-2:hyperpara.q: Brown tumors in hyperparathyroidism consist of:
endo-patho-2:hyperpara.e: Osteitis fibrosa cystica: brown color from hemorrhage and hemosiderin.

endo-patho-2:hyperpara.q: A 58-year-old woman has kidney stones, constipation and low mood. Calcium is 11.4 mg/dL, phosphate 2.1 mg/dL, PTH 128 pg/mL and 24-h urine calcium is high. Sestamibi scan shows one focus near the left lower thyroid pole. Histology of the lesion would most likely show:
o: Chief cells with little stromal fat
endo-patho-2:hyperpara.e: Parathyroid adenoma: chief cells, inconspicuous fat, compressed rim.

endo-patho-2:fhh.q: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia is caused by:
o: Overexpression of cyclin D1 in chief cells
Inactivation of the maternal GNAS allele
endo-patho-2:fhh.e: Higher calcium is needed to suppress PTH; kidneys reabsorb more calcium.

endo-patho-2:fhh.q: A calcium/creatinine clearance ratio below 0.01 favors:
endo-patho-2:fhh.e: Primary hyperparathyroidism usually gives a ratio above 0.02.

endo-patho-2:fhh.q: A 27-year-old man has a calcium of 10.9 mg/dL on routine labs. He has no symptoms. PTH is 58 pg/mL and 24-h urine calcium is low. His mother and sister have mild hypercalcemia. The best management is:
endo-patho-2:fhh.e: FHH is benign; parathyroid surgery does not help.

endo-patho-2:hyperca-wu.q: The most common cause of symptomatic hypercalcemia in hospitalized adults is:
endo-patho-2:hyperca-wu.e: Primary hyperparathyroidism is the most common cause of asymptomatic hypercalcemia.

endo-patho-2:hyperca-wu.q: Hypercalcemia in sarcoidosis is caused by:

A 66-year-old smoker has confusion and polyuria. Calcium is 14.2 mg/dL, PTH 6 pg/mL and PTHrP elevated. Chest CT shows a central cavitating mass. After intravenous saline, which drug gives the most durable control of calcium?
endo-patho-2:hyperca-wu.e: Squamous cell carcinoma with HHM; bisphosphonates block bone resorption.

endo-patho-2:dm-dx.q: Which value meets a diagnostic criterion for diabetes mellitus?
endo-patho-2:dm-dx.e: Thresholds: FPG ≥ 126, OGTT ≥ 200, HbA1c ≥ 6.5%, random ≥ 200 with symptoms.

endo-patho-2:dm-dx.q: A fasting plasma glucose of 112 mg/dL is classified as:
A 55-year-old man is admitted with pneumonia and a glucose of 190 mg/dL. He has no diabetes history; HbA1c is 5.6%. The best interpretation is:
endo-patho-2:dm-dx.e: Catecholamines and cortisol raise glucose transiently; persistence is required.

endo-patho-2:dm-meta.q: Ketoacidosis is uncommon in type 2 diabetes because:
o: Free fatty acids cannot reach the liver at all
Muscle oxidizes ketones faster in obese patients
Glucagon secretion is absent in type 2 disease
Portal insulin still restrains hepatic ketogenesis

endo-patho-2:dm-meta.q: Polyuria in uncontrolled diabetes is primarily due to:
endo-patho-2:dm-meta.e: Glucose above the renal threshold drags water, Na⁺ and K⁺.

endo-patho-2:dm-meta.q: A 15-year-old girl has lost 5 kg despite eating more, with constant thirst and nocturia for 6 weeks. Today she is vomiting and breathing deeply. Which process directly explains the deep breathing?

endo-patho-2:t1-t2.q: Islet amyloid deposition is characteristic of:
Identical-twin concordance is higher in type 2 diabetes because:
endo-patho-2:t1-t2.e: About 90% for type 2 vs about 50% for type 1.

endo-patho-2:t1-t2.q: A 9-year-old girl presents with polyuria and weight loss. Antibodies against glutamic acid decarboxylase are positive. A pancreatic biopsy at onset would show:
o: Amyloid replacing most of the islets
T cells and macrophages infiltrating islets
Increased number and size of islets
endo-patho-2:t1-t2.e: Insulitis precedes β-cell depletion in type 1.

endo-patho-2:dka-hhs.q: In DKA, the serum potassium is often normal or high even though:
endo-patho-2:dka-hhs.e: Acidosis and insulin lack shift K⁺ out of cells; urine losses deplete stores.

endo-patho-2:dka-hhs.q: Compared with DKA, HHS is characterized by:
o: Kussmaul breathing with a fruity breath odor
Rapid onset over a few hours in young patients
Lower glucose with a marked anion gap acidosis
endo-patho-2:dka-hhs.e: Glucose often > 600 mg/dL and osmolality > 320 mOsm/kg.

endo-patho-2:dka-hhs.q: A 21-year-old man with type 1 diabetes has glucose 520 mg/dL, pH 7.08, bicarbonate 7 mEq/L, anion gap 28 and K⁺ 3.0 mEq/L. Intravenous saline has been started. The next step is:
endo-patho-2:dka-hhs.e: Insulin would drive K⁺ lower; correct K⁺ < 3.3 first.

endo-patho-2:dm-comp.q: The most common cause of death in diabetes mellitus is:
Cataracts in diabetes are linked to accumulation of sorbitol produced by:
A 61-year-old man with 20 years of type 2 diabetes has early satiety and vomits undigested food eaten hours earlier. He also has burning feet. The vomiting is best explained by:
o: Gastric outlet obstruction by peptic scarring
endo-patho-2:dm-comp.e: Autonomic neuropathy: gastroparesis, diabetic diarrhea, GERD.

endo-patho-2:hypogly.q: The first physiologic defense as glucose falls is:
endo-patho-2:hypogly.e: Insulin falls at about 80–85 mg/dL, before glucagon and epinephrine rise.

endo-patho-2:hypogly.q: A 70-year-old man with type 1 diabetes on insulin and propranolol is found confused and sweaty but without tremor or palpitations. Fingerstick glucose is 38 mg/dL and he cannot swallow safely. The best immediate treatment is:
endo-patho-2:hypogly.e: Glucagon IM or IV dextrose when oral intake is unsafe.

endo-patho-2:dm-kidney.q: The earliest clinical sign of diabetic nephropathy is:

A 48-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes for 25 years has proteinuria of 4 g/day. Biopsy shows thickened capillary basement membranes, mesangial expansion and hyaline thickening of both afferent and efferent arterioles. The vascular change is called:
endo-patho-2:dm-kidney.e: Hyaline arteriolosclerosis is more severe in diabetes than in hypertension alone.

endo-patho-3:cushing.q: The most common cause of Cushing syndrome overall is:
endo-patho-3:cushing.e: Cushing disease is the most common endogenous cause.

endo-patho-3:cushing.q: In Cushing syndrome caused by a cortisol-secreting adrenal adenoma, the contralateral adrenal cortex is:

A 58-year-old man with a 60 pack-year history has rapidly progressive weakness, hypertension, hypokalemia and darkening skin over 2 months. Cortisol and ACTH are both very high. The adrenal glands would most likely show:
endo-patho-3:cushing.e: Ectopic ACTH (small cell carcinoma) drives both glands.

endo-patho-3:cush-wu.e: Others include late-night salivary cortisol and the 1 mg overnight DST.

endo-patho-3:cush-wu.q: High ACTH with cortisol suppression after high-dose dexamethasone indicates:
A 34-year-old woman has central obesity, purple striae and hypertension. Late-night salivary cortisol is high on two occasions and plasma ACTH is undetectable. The next step is:
endo-patho-3:cush-wu.e: ACTH-independent: look for an adrenal tumor (after excluding steroid use).

endo-patho-3:adrenal-insuf.q: Hyperkalemia occurs in primary but not secondary adrenal insufficiency because in secondary disease:
o: The kidney becomes resistant to aldosterone
endo-patho-3:adrenal-insuf.e: Zona glomerulosa does not depend on ACTH.

endo-patho-3:adrenal-insuf.q: The most common cause of tertiary adrenal insufficiency is:
o: Autoimmune destruction of the adrenal cortex
Infarction of the pituitary after delivery

endo-patho-3:adrenal-insuf.q: A 7-year-old boy has fever, a spreading petechial rash and hypotension unresponsive to fluids. Blood cultures grow gram-negative diplococci. At autopsy both adrenals are converted to sacs of clotted blood. This is:
endo-patho-3:adrenal-insuf.e: Meningococcemia with DIC and bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.

endo-patho-3:aldo.q: Patients with primary hyperaldosteronism usually do not develop edema because of:
endo-patho-3:aldo.e: Pressure natriuresis and ANP limit volume expansion.

endo-patho-3:aldo.q: A 44-year-old woman has hypertension resistant to three drugs, K⁺ 3.1 mEq/L and a high aldosterone/renin ratio confirmed by saline suppression. CT shows a 1.4-cm left adrenal nodule and adrenal vein sampling lateralizes left. The best treatment is:
endo-patho-3:aldo.e: Aldosterone-producing adenoma (Conn) is surgically curable; bilateral hyperplasia is treated medically.

endo-patho-3:cah.q: The most common form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia is deficiency of:
Hypertension with virilization in a girl suggests deficiency of:
endo-patho-3:cah.e: 11-deoxycorticosterone accumulates and acts as a mineralocorticoid.

endo-patho-3:cah.q: A 10-day-old boy has vomiting, poor feeding and dehydration. Na⁺ is 124 mEq/L and K⁺ 7.0 mEq/L. Which serum finding is expected?

endo-patho-3:incidentaloma.q: Before biopsy or surgery of any adrenal mass, which must be excluded?
An adrenal mass with attenuation below 10 HU on unenhanced CT is most likely a:
endo-patho-3:incidentaloma.e: Carcinomas and pheochromocytomas usually exceed 20 HU.

endo-patho-3:incidentaloma.q: A 61-year-old woman has a 2.4-cm adrenal mass found on CT for kidney stones. It measures 6 HU. Blood pressure and potassium are normal. Which hormone test is recommended for every patient like her?
endo-patho-3:incidentaloma.e: Screens for mild autonomous cortisol secretion; other tests depend on HU, BP and suspicion.

endo-patho-3:net.q: Which marker is characteristic of neuroendocrine tumors?
The nuclear chromatin of well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors is described as:
A 52-year-old man has a 1.5-cm ileal mass composed of nests of uniform cells with stippled chromatin that stain for synaptophysin. Ki-67 is 2%. The tumor is best classified as a:
endo-patho-3:net.e: Formerly called carcinoid; low proliferation index.

endo-patho-3:neuroblastoma.e: Adrenal medulla or anywhere along the sympathetic chain.

endo-patho-3:neuroblastoma.q: The strongest adverse prognostic marker in neuroblastoma is:
endo-patho-3:neuroblastoma.e: It places the tumor in the high-risk group regardless of stage.

endo-patho-3:neuroblastoma.q: A 2-year-old boy has a firm, irregular abdominal mass crossing the midline and rapid, chaotic eye movements with jerking limbs. Blood pressure is normal. Which urine finding is expected?

endo-patho-3:pheo.q: Before resection of a pheochromocytoma, blood pressure should first be controlled with:
endo-patho-3:pheo.e: α-blockade before β-blockade to avoid unopposed α stimulation.

endo-patho-3:pheo.q: The nests of chief cells surrounded by S-100-positive sustentacular cells in pheochromocytoma are called:
endo-patho-3:pheo.e: Chief cells stain for chromogranin and synaptophysin.

endo-patho-3:pheo.q: A 36-year-old woman has episodes of pounding headache, sweating and palpitations with BP up to 230/130 mm Hg. Her brother has a thyroid cancer that secretes calcitonin. Which gene is most likely mutated?
endo-patho-3:pheo.e: MEN2A: pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid carcinoma.

endo-patho-3:men.q: MEN1 is caused by mutation of:
Which feature distinguishes MEN2B from MEN2A?
endo-patho-3:men.e: MEN2B also has marfanoid habitus and lacks hyperparathyroidism.

endo-patho-3:men.q: A 38-year-old man has recurrent duodenal ulcers despite PPIs, a calcium of 11.6 mg/dL with high PTH, and a history of galactorrhea treated with cabergoline. The most frequent first manifestation of his syndrome is:
endo-patho-3:men.e: MEN1: parathyroid disease appears in 80–95% and usually first.

endo-patho-3:islet.q: Which laboratory pair indicates an insulinoma rather than exogenous insulin?
Necrolytic migratory erythema with new diabetes suggests a tumor of:

A 44-year-old woman has spells of confusion and diplopia before breakfast that resolve after juice. During a supervised fast, glucose is 41 mg/dL with insulin and C-peptide inappropriately high. A screen for oral hypoglycemic agents is negative. The most likely diagnosis is:

endo-patho-3:carcinoid.q: Carcinoid syndrome from an intestinal primary usually indicates:
endo-patho-3:carcinoid.e: Hepatic first-pass metabolism otherwise inactivates serotonin.

endo-patho-3:carcinoid.q: The cardiac lesion of carcinoid syndrome typically involves the:
endo-patho-3:carcinoid.e: Lung MAO protects the left heart.

endo-patho-3:carcinoid.q: A 59-year-old man has episodic facial flushing, watery diarrhea and wheezing. Examination reveals a holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border and nodular hepatomegaly. He later develops dermatitis and confusion. Which deficiency explains the late findings?
endo-patho-3:carcinoid.e: Tryptophan is diverted to serotonin, causing pellagra.

endo-patho-3:zes.q: The most common location of gastrinomas is the:
In Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, the secretin stimulation test shows:
A 46-year-old woman has multiple jejunal ulcers despite high-dose PPI, plus diarrhea with steatorrhea. Fasting gastrin is very high. Why does she have steatorrhea?
o: Bile acids are lost through ulcer perforation
Gastrin directly damages enterocyte brush borders
Acid inactivates pancreatic lipase in the small bowel
endo-patho-3:zes.e: Low intestinal pH inactivates pancreatic enzymes.

endo-patho-3:aps.q: APS-1 is caused by mutation of:
endo-patho-3:aps.e: Defective thymic expression of peripheral self-antigens.

endo-patho-3:aps.q: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis in APS-1 is linked to autoantibodies against:
endo-patho-3:aps.e: Th17 effector cytokines defend against fungi.

endo-patho-3:aps.q: A 14-year-old girl with lifelong oral thrush and dystrophic nails had hypocalcemic seizures at age 9. She now has fatigue, salt craving and darkening of her gums. Her next most likely laboratory abnormality is:
endo-patho-3:aps.e: APS-1: candidiasis → hypoparathyroidism → primary adrenal insufficiency.

endo-physio-1:hp.q: Hypothalamic releasing hormones reach the anterior pituitary mainly through the:
endo-physio-1:hp.e: Releasing hormones are secreted into the median eminence and carried by portal vessels straight to anterior pituitary sinusoids.

endo-physio-1:hp.q: Which hormone shares a common α-subunit with TSH, LH and FSH?
endo-physio-1:hp.e: TSH, LH, FSH and hCG share the α-subunit; the β-subunit confers specificity.

endo-physio-1:hp.q: A 45-year-old woman develops darkening of the skin together with weight gain and proximal weakness. Her plasma ACTH is high. The pigmentation is best explained by:
o: Prolactin co-secreted by the same adenoma
Aldosterone excess in the zona glomerulosa
MSH cleaved from the same POMC precursor
endo-physio-1:hp.e: POMC is processed into ACTH, MSH and β-endorphin, so ACTH excess comes with MSH.

endo-physio-1:gh.q: Most of the growth-promoting effect of GH on cartilage is mediated by:
o: IGF-1 produced mainly by the liver
Direct binding of GH to chondrocytes only
Cortisol released from the adrenal cortex
endo-physio-1:gh.e: GH stimulates hepatic IGF-1 (somatomedin C), which drives chondrocyte proliferation.

endo-physio-1:gh.q: Which condition normally increases growth hormone secretion?
endo-physio-1:gh.e: Hypoglycemia, deep sleep, exercise, stress and fasting stimulate GH; hyperglycemia, obesity and IGF-1 inhibit it.

endo-physio-1:gh.q: A 40-year-old man with a GH-secreting pituitary adenoma has a fasting glucose of 140 mg/dL. The hyperglycemia is best explained by GH causing:
o: Insulin resistance with more hepatic glucose output
Increased renal reabsorption of filtered glucose
Destruction of pancreatic β cells by antibodies
Inhibition of glucagon release from α cells
endo-physio-1:gh.e: GH is diabetogenic: it reduces muscle glucose uptake and raises hepatic gluconeogenesis.

endo-physio-1:adh.q: ADH increases water permeability of the collecting duct by acting through:
o: V1 receptors, cAMP and urea transporters
V1 receptors, IP₃ and aquaporin-2 insertion
V2 receptors, cAMP and aquaporin-2 insertion
V2 receptors, IP₃ and ENaC insertion
endo-physio-1:adh.e: V2 → Gs → cAMP → PKA → AQP2 vesicles fuse with the apical membrane.

endo-physio-1:adh.q: Compared with a normal person, volume depletion changes the ADH–osmolality relation by:
o: Leaving the curve unchanged at all levels
Shifting the threshold lower and steepening it
Shifting the threshold higher and flattening it
endo-physio-1:adh.e: Hypovolemia lowers the osmotic threshold and increases the slope, so ADH is released even at low osmolality.

endo-physio-1:adh.q: A 30-year-old man has polyuria after a head injury. Urine osmolality is 120 mOsm/kg and rises to 600 mOsm/kg after desmopressin. Which defect best explains his findings?
o: Excess water intake suppressing ADH release
Osmotic diuresis caused by glucose in urine
Collecting duct cells unresponsive to ADH
Deficient ADH release from the posterior pituitary
endo-physio-1:adh.e: Response to desmopressin indicates AVP deficiency (central DI), not AVP resistance.

endo-physio-1:prl.q: Prolactin secretion from the anterior pituitary is tonically inhibited by:
endo-physio-1:prl.e: Dopamine from the arcuate (tuberoinfundibular) neurons is prolactin-inhibiting factor.

endo-physio-1:prl.q: Lactational amenorrhea is mainly caused by prolactin suppressing:
endo-physio-1:prl.e: Prolactin (and the suckling reflex) inhibit GnRH, lowering LH and FSH.

endo-physio-1:prl.q: A 26-year-old woman taking risperidone has amenorrhea and milky nipple discharge. Her prolactin level is elevated. The mechanism is blockade of:
endo-physio-1:prl.e: Antipsychotics remove dopamine's tonic inhibition of lactotrophs.

endo-physio-1:thsyn.q: Iodide enters the thyroid follicular cell from blood through the:
endo-physio-1:thsyn.e: NIS on the basolateral membrane moves 2 Na⁺ with 1 I⁻; pendrin moves I⁻ into the colloid.

endo-physio-1:thsyn.q: T₄ is formed within thyroglobulin by coupling of:
endo-physio-1:thsyn.e: DIT + DIT = T₄; MIT + DIT = T₃.

endo-physio-1:thsyn.q: A patient with Graves disease is started on methimazole. Which step of thyroid hormone synthesis is directly inhibited?
o: Endocytosis of colloid by follicular cells
Conversion of T₄ to T₃ in the liver
Iodide uptake by the Na⁺/I⁻ symporter
endo-physio-1:thsyn.e: Thionamides block TPO-mediated oxidation, organification and coupling.

endo-physio-1:threg.q: Most circulating T₃ is produced by:
o: Conversion of reverse T₃ in liver
endo-physio-1:threg.e: About three quarters of circulating T₃ comes from peripheral 5′-deiodination of T₄ (liver, kidney).

endo-physio-1:threg.q: The deiodinase that converts T₄ to T₃ in the pituitary, mediating TSH feedback, is:
endo-physio-1:threg.e: D2 in pituitary and CNS supplies local T₃; D3 forms reverse T₃.

endo-physio-1:threg.q: A 29-year-old woman who is 12 weeks pregnant has a high total T₄, normal free T₄ and normal TSH. The most likely explanation is:
endo-physio-1:threg.e: Estrogen raises TBG, increasing total but not free hormone.

endo-physio-1:threg.q: A 70-year-old man in the ICU with septic shock has a low T₃, high reverse T₃, and normal TSH and T₄. These findings are best explained by:
o: Loss of TSH from pituitary infarction
Primary failure of the thyroid gland
endo-physio-1:threg.e: Nonthyroidal illness lowers 5′-deiodinase activity; rT₃ rises because its clearance falls.

endo-physio-1:thact.q: Thyroid hormone raises basal metabolic rate largely by increasing:
endo-physio-1:thact.e: T₃ induces Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase and increases mitochondrial number and activity, raising O₂ use.

endo-physio-1:thact.q: The thyroid hormone receptor binds DNA mainly as a heterodimer with the:
endo-physio-1:thact.e: TR–RXR heterodimers sit on thyroid response elements.

endo-physio-1:thact.q: A 34-year-old woman has palpitations, tremor, heat intolerance and a resting heart rate of 118/min. Propranolol relieves her palpitations quickly because excess thyroid hormone:
o: Stimulates renin release from the kidney
endo-physio-1:thact.e: Catecholamine levels are normal; tissue sensitivity rises through more β receptors.

endo-physio-1:pth.q: PTH secretion is regulated primarily by plasma ionized Ca²⁺ acting on the:
endo-physio-1:pth.e: CaSR is a Gq-coupled receptor on chief cells; high Ca²⁺ suppresses PTH.

endo-physio-1:pth.q: PTH stimulates osteoclast activity indirectly by causing osteoblasts to release:
endo-physio-1:pth.e: RANKL from osteoblasts/osteocytes binds RANK on osteoclast precursors.

endo-physio-1:pth.q: A 52-year-old woman with chronic alcohol use has a serum Ca²⁺ of 6.8 mg/dL that does not improve with IV calcium. Her Mg²⁺ is 0.7 mg/dL and PTH is inappropriately low. Which step corrects the calcium?
o: Giving phosphate to raise bone deposition
Giving calcitriol to block PTH release
Giving a loop diuretic to retain calcium
Giving magnesium to restore PTH secretion
endo-physio-1:pth.e: Severe hypomagnesemia impairs PTH secretion and action; Mg repletion corrects it.

endo-physio-1:ca.q: About what fraction of plasma calcium is ionized (free)?
endo-physio-1:ca.e: Roughly 45% free, 40% albumin-bound, 15% complexed with anions (FA).

endo-physio-1:ca.q: Acute respiratory alkalosis tends to cause tetany because it:
endo-physio-1:ca.e: Fewer H⁺ on albumin leaves more sites for Ca²⁺, lowering ionized Ca²⁺.

endo-physio-1:ca.q: A 66-year-old woman with cirrhosis has total calcium 7.6 mg/dL and albumin 2.0 g/dL. She has no paresthesias and her PTH is normal. Her ionized calcium is most likely:
endo-physio-1:ca.e: Hypoalbuminemia lowers total calcium but leaves ionized Ca²⁺ (and PTH) unchanged.

endo-physio-1:vitd.q: The 1α-hydroxylation that activates vitamin D occurs in the:
endo-physio-1:vitd.e: Liver forms 25(OH)D; the PCT adds the 1α-hydroxyl group.

endo-physio-1:vitd.q: Fibroblast growth factor 23 lowers serum phosphate mainly by:
o: Increasing PTH secretion from chief cells
Reducing NaPi transporters in proximal tubule
endo-physio-1:vitd.e: FGF23 (from osteocytes) reduces NaPi-IIa/IIc and suppresses 1α-hydroxylase.

endo-physio-1:vitd.q: A 58-year-old man with stage 4 CKD has high phosphate, low calcitriol and very high PTH. Which hormone, made by osteocytes and elevated early in CKD, contributes to his low calcitriol?
endo-physio-1:vitd.e: Phosphate retention raises FGF23, which inhibits renal 1α-hydroxylase.

endo-physio-1:calcit.e: C cells (from the 4th pharyngeal pouch) secrete calcitonin when Ca²⁺ rises.

o: Stimulating PTH release from chief cells
endo-physio-1:calcit.e: Calcitonin acts mainly on osteoclasts; its effect in adults is small and transient.

endo-physio-1:calcit.q: Six months after total thyroidectomy with parathyroid preservation, a 44-year-old woman has a normal serum calcium. This is best explained by:
o: Reduced vitamin D intake after surgery
Increased calcitonin from ectopic C cells
PTH control that overrides loss of calcitonin
endo-physio-1:calcit.e: Calcitonin has little long-term role in adult calcium homeostasis; PTH dominates.

endo-physio-2:glucagon.q: Glucagon raises blood glucose within minutes mainly by stimulating hepatic:
o: Glycogen synthesis through PI3K and Akt
endo-physio-2:glucagon.e: Glucagon receptor → Gs → cAMP → PKA → phosphorylase activation.

endo-physio-2:glucagon.q: A high-protein meal with little carbohydrate causes plasma insulin and glucagon to:
endo-physio-2:glucagon.e: Amino acids (alanine, arginine) stimulate both hormones, preventing hypoglycemia.

endo-physio-2:glucagon.q: After an overnight fast and 4 hours of glucagon infusion, a volunteer's liver glycogen is depleted but blood glucose stays high. Which process maintains it?
endo-physio-2:glucagon.e: Glucagon increases amino acid uptake and gluconeogenesis once glycogen is exhausted.

endo-physio-2:insulin.q: The rate-limiting step for glucose sensing in the pancreatic β cell is catalyzed by:
endo-physio-2:insulin.e: Glucokinase phosphorylation of glucose sets ATP production and insulin release.

endo-physio-2:insulin.q: In the β cell, a rise in ATP/ADP ratio triggers insulin release by:
o: Activating Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase to depolarize the cell
Opening K_ATP channels and hyperpolarizing the cell
Closing K_ATP channels and depolarizing the cell
endo-physio-2:insulin.e: Depolarization opens voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels; Ca²⁺ influx drives exocytosis.

endo-physio-2:insulin.q: A 40-year-old nurse has recurrent hypoglycemia with high insulin and a very low C-peptide. The most likely source of her insulin is:
endo-physio-2:insulin.e: Endogenous insulin is secreted 1:1 with C-peptide; injected insulin lacks it.

endo-physio-2:insulin.q: A man with type 2 diabetes on glyburide becomes hypoglycemic after skipping lunch. The drug caused insulin release despite low glucose because it:
o: Increases glucokinase activity in β cells
Enhances incretin release from the gut
Increases GLUT2 expression in β cells
Closes K_ATP channels independently of ATP
endo-physio-2:insulin.e: Sulfonylureas bind SUR1 and close K_ATP channels regardless of glucose.

endo-physio-2:insact.q: The insulin receptor transmits its signal through:
o: Janus kinase associated with the receptor
Guanylyl cyclase in the receptor domain
A stimulatory G protein and cAMP
endo-physio-2:insact.e: The β subunits autophosphorylate tyrosines and recruit IRS proteins.

endo-physio-2:insact.q: Which tissue requires insulin for most of its glucose uptake?
endo-physio-2:insact.e: Muscle and fat use insulin-dependent GLUT4; brain, RBC and liver do not.

endo-physio-2:insact.q: A 17-year-old with type 1 diabetes in ketoacidosis has a serum K⁺ of 5.9 mEq/L. After IV insulin, serum K⁺ falls to 3.6 mEq/L. Insulin lowered K⁺ by:
endo-physio-2:insact.e: Insulin drives K⁺ into cells via Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase.

endo-physio-2:ogtt.q: The greater insulin response to oral glucose than to IV glucose giving the same plasma glucose is due to:
o: Incretins such as GLP-1 and GIP
Faster glucose absorption from the gut
endo-physio-2:ogtt.e: Gut incretins amplify glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.

endo-physio-2:ogtt.q: The first phase of insulin release after an IV glucose bolus comes from:
endo-physio-2:ogtt.e: The 2–5 minute acute phase releases docked, presynthesized insulin.

endo-physio-2:ogtt.q: A 52-year-old obese man has fasting glucose 118 mg/dL and a 2-hour OGTT glucose of 215 mg/dL. His insulin rises slowly but reaches a high peak. Which early β-cell defect is typical of his condition?
endo-physio-2:ogtt.e: Loss of first-phase secretion is an early defect in type 2 diabetes.

endo-physio-2:cah.q: The rate-limiting step of adrenal steroid synthesis is:
endo-physio-2:cah.e: StAR-mediated cholesterol transfer and SCC (desmolase) set the rate.

endo-physio-2:cah.q: Aldosterone is made only in the zona glomerulosa because that zone uniquely expresses:
endo-physio-2:cah.e: Aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) is glomerulosa specific; the zone also lacks 17α-hydroxylase.

endo-physio-2:cah.q: A 10-day-old girl with ambiguous genitalia has vomiting, Na⁺ 126 mEq/L and K⁺ 6.8 mEq/L. Which serum steroid is most likely elevated?
endo-physio-2:cah.e: 21-hydroxylase deficiency: salt wasting with 17-OHP accumulation and androgen excess.

endo-physio-2:cah.q: A 16-year-old phenotypic girl has hypertension, hypokalemia, absent breast development and primary amenorrhea. Karyotype is 46,XY. Which enzyme is deficient?
endo-physio-2:cah.e: 17α-hydroxylase deficiency: no cortisol or sex steroids, DOC excess causes hypertension.

endo-physio-2:cortisol.q: Most circulating cortisol is bound to:
endo-physio-2:cortisol.e: About 90–95% of cortisol is protein bound, mainly to CBG (transcortin).

endo-physio-2:cortisol.q: Plasma cortisol in a healthy person is highest:
endo-physio-2:cortisol.e: ACTH and cortisol follow a circadian rhythm peaking before waking.

endo-physio-2:cortisol.q: A 38-year-old woman taking prednisone for 6 months has a white count with low eosinophils and low lymphocytes but high neutrophils. The neutrophilia is mainly due to glucocorticoids:
o: Increasing histamine release from mast cells
Increasing IL-5 release from T cells
endo-physio-2:cortisol.e: Glucocorticoids inhibit leukocyte adhesion (demargination) while lowering eosinophils and lymphocytes.

endo-physio-2:appetite.q: Leptin reduces food intake mainly by:
o: Stimulating ghrelin release from the stomach
Blocking melanocortin-4 receptors in the PVN
Inhibiting POMC neurons and stimulating NPY neurons
Stimulating POMC neurons and inhibiting NPY neurons
endo-physio-2:appetite.e: Leptin activates anorexigenic POMC/CART and suppresses NPY/AgRP neurons.

endo-physio-2:appetite.q: Ghrelin is secreted mainly by the stomach and:
endo-physio-2:appetite.e: Ghrelin rises before meals, acts on the GH secretagogue receptor and stimulates hunger.

endo-physio-2:appetite.q: A 4-year-old boy with severe early-onset obesity and constant hunger has undetectable serum leptin. Which treatment addresses his underlying defect?
endo-physio-2:appetite.e: Congenital leptin deficiency causes hyperphagia; leptin replacement corrects it.

endo-physio-2:signal.q: Which hormone acts through a Gq–phospholipase C–IP₃ pathway?
endo-physio-2:signal.e: GnRH, oxytocin, ADH (V1), TRH, H1, angiotensin II and gastrin use IP₃ (GOAT HAG).

endo-physio-2:signal.q: Growth hormone and prolactin receptors signal mainly through:
o: Associated JAK kinases and STAT proteins
Adenylyl cyclase and protein kinase A
endo-physio-2:signal.e: These cytokine-family receptors lack intrinsic kinase activity and use JAK2.

endo-physio-2:signal.q: A drug that increases cGMP in vascular smooth muscle would mimic the action of:
endo-physio-2:signal.e: ANP/BNP and NO raise cGMP and cause vasodilation and natriuresis.

endo-physio-2:steroid.q: Which hormone acts mainly through an intracellular receptor?
endo-physio-2:steroid.e: Steroids, T₃/T₄ and vitamin D bind intracellular receptors (PET CAT in TV).

endo-physio-2:steroid.q: In plasma, the fraction of testosterone that is free (unbound) is about:
endo-physio-2:steroid.e: About 45% binds SHBG, most of the rest albumin; only ~2% is free.

endo-physio-2:steroid.q: A 30-year-old man with Graves disease develops tender breast enlargement. His total testosterone is normal. The gynecomastia is best explained by increased:
endo-physio-2:steroid.e: Hyperthyroidism raises SHBG, lowering free testosterone relative to free estradiol.

endo-physio-2:stress.q: As plasma glucose falls, the first physiologic defense against hypoglycemia is:
endo-physio-2:stress.e: Insulin falls at ~80–85 mg/dL, before glucagon and epinephrine rise at ~65–70.

endo-physio-2:stress.q: Compared with epinephrine, cortisol's effect on blood glucose is:
endo-physio-2:stress.e: Cortisol and GH act through gene expression and take hours; epinephrine acts within minutes.

endo-physio-2:stress.q: A 25-year-old man with long-standing type 1 diabetes has lost his glucagon response to hypoglycemia. Which hormone becomes his most important rapid defense against falling glucose?
endo-physio-2:stress.e: Epinephrine is the third defense and becomes critical when glucagon is deficient.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: น้ำตาลสูงน้ำหนักเกิน
title.en: Boss case: High sugar, heavy heart

boss.case: A 56-year-old man with obesity (BMI 34), hypertension and a prior MI has HbA1c 8.6%. eGFR 75. He is not on any diabetes medication.

qs.q: First-line drug for most patients with type 2 diabetes:
qs.e: Unless contraindicated; weight neutral, no hypoglycemia.
Avoid in severe renal impairment and with iodinated contrast.

qs.q: Given his established atherosclerotic disease, which add-on reduces cardiovascular events?
qs.e: Liraglutide/semaglutide and empagliflozin have proven CV benefit.
Glucosuria predisposes to UTIs and candidiasis.

qs.q: Which drug class is contraindicated in medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2?

title.th: ทารกอาเจียน ขาดน้ำ

stem.th: ทารกอายุ 10 วัน อาเจียน ซึม น้ำหนักลด อวัยวะเพศกำกวม (clitoromegaly, labia เชื่อมกัน) โครโมโซม 46,XX
stem.en: A 10-day-old with vomiting, lethargy and weight loss has ambiguous genitalia (clitoromegaly, fused labia); karyotype 46,XX.

steps.q: The deficient enzyme is most likely:
steps.e: Salt wasting with virilization of a 46,XX infant: no aldosterone or cortisol, so precursors shunt to androgens. 11β-hydroxylase deficiency virilizes but causes hypertension (11-deoxycorticosterone).

info.th: Na⁺ 126, K⁺ 7.1 mEq/L, glucose ต่ำ

steps.q: The serum marker that confirms it is a raised:
steps.e: 17-OH-progesterone is the substrate of 21-hydroxylase and accumulates; newborn screening measures it.

steps.q: Hydrocortisone reduces the androgen excess mainly by:
steps.e: Low cortisol removes feedback, so ACTH drives adrenal hyperplasia and androgen output; replacing cortisol switches ACTH off.

info.th: ให้ hydrocortisone แล้ว ACTH ลดลง

steps.q: She also needs fludrocortisone because it:
o: Raises cortisol binding to plasma CBG
Blocks the action of excess androgens
steps.e: Salt-wasting forms lack aldosterone, so a mineralocorticoid (acting on the mineralocorticoid receptor) is added to correct hyponatremia and hyperkalemia.

title.th: ชาปลายนิ้วหลังผ่าตัดไทรอยด์

stem.th: หญิง 45 ปี วันที่ 2 หลังผ่าตัด total thyroidectomy ชารอบปากและปลายนิ้ว กล้ามเนื้อเกร็ง
stem.en: On day 2 after total thyroidectomy, a 45-year-old woman has perioral and fingertip tingling and muscle cramps.

o: Removal or ischemia of the parathyroids
Excess calcitonin released from the thyroid
steps.e: Parathyroid injury is the classic cause of hypocalcemia after total thyroidectomy; calcitonin has little effect on Ca²⁺ in humans.

info.th: แตะหน้าหู กล้ามเนื้อหน้ากระตุก (Chvostek +) · Ca²⁺ 6.8 mg/dL, albumin ปกติ
info.en: Tapping in front of the ear makes the face twitch (Chvostek sign) · Ca²⁺ 6.8 mg/dL, normal albumin

steps.q: Low ionized Ca²⁺ causes tetany because it:
o: Lowers the threshold of nerve Na⁺ channels
Blocks acetylcholine release at the NMJ
steps.e: Less extracellular Ca²⁺ makes Na⁺ channels open more easily, so nerves fire spontaneously.

steps.q: Phosphate is high because, without PTH, the kidney:
o: Keeps more NaPi-IIa in the proximal tubule
Excretes more phosphate in the distal tubule
Secretes more FGF23 into the plasma
steps.e: PTH normally removes NaPi-IIa from the proximal tubule; without it phosphate reabsorption rises.

info.th: ผลเลือด: PTH ต่ำ, phosphate สูง

steps.q: Long-term, she needs calcium plus which vitamin D form?
steps.e: Without PTH, renal 1α-hydroxylase is not stimulated, so the active form must be given.

title.th: ใจสั่น น้ำหนักลด ตาโปน

stem.th: หญิง 30 ปี ใจสั่น เหงื่อออก น้ำหนักลด 5 kg ตาโปน คอโตแบบ diffuse
stem.en: A 30-year-old woman has palpitations, sweating, 5-kg weight loss, proptosis and a diffuse goiter.

info.th: TSH ต่ำมาก, free T₄ สูง, TRAb +
info.en: TSH suppressed, free T₄ high, TSH-receptor antibodies positive

steps.e: PTU is reserved for 1st trimester and thyroid storm.

o: Start oral antibiotics and continue methimazole
Stop methimazole; check CBC with differential
Increase methimazole and recheck free T₄

info.th: 2 เดือนต่อมา มีไข้ เจ็บคอ
info.en: Two months later she has fever and sore throat

steps.e: Recheck TSH 6–8 weeks after dose changes.

info.th: หลังรักษาด้วย radioiodine กลายเป็น hypothyroid

dx.e: Most common functioning adenoma; dopamine agonists shrink it.

dx.e: Maternal GNAS mutation; end-organ PTH resistance.

dx.e: Corticotroph microadenoma; MRI pituitary.

dx.e: Autoimmune destruction of the adrenal cortex.
